question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says 'When a cast door refuses, runs raise a trouble and re-raise instead of writing the ticket, leaving the red new for a later run to retry', but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The clause states 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds'. If the ticket is built, some runs encounter new reds but fail to write tickets (when the door refuses). The outline provides no exception for door refusals—only 'unless one is already open'. This violates the stated requirement that each run writes tickets for reds it finds.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands, and the ticket meets it. The ticket creates no run that skips the write: every run still calls the door for every new red (cairn/devices/tester/device.py:1007). A door refusing is the defect, and it happens today, measured 2026-11-23 on akiendell, where it left nothing on disk. This ticket makes that defect loud and lasting. The run fails rather than completing (falsifier clause 2), a trouble names the door and its lacks so someone can fix the door (clause 1), and the next run tries the ticket again until it lands (clause 3). There is no exception to 9.4.2.3.7.5 here; this is how a refusal stops hiding the fact that it was broken (constraint 5, same as open-67977da252c0).
